read.title: A shared map of the body
text: Anatomy needs a language that means the same thing to everyone, no matter how a person happens to be standing or lying. The solution is anatomical position: upright, facing forward, feet together, arms at the sides, palms forward. Every directional term is defined against this posture, even when the person is actually lying on a table.

The terms come in opposite pairs. Anterior and posterior mean front and back. Superior and inferior mean toward or away from the head. Medial and lateral mean toward or away from the midline. Proximal and distal apply mainly to limbs and compare distance from the trunk, so the wrist is distal to the elbow. Superficial and deep compare distance from the body surface.

Planes describe how the body is cut. A sagittal plane separates right from left, a frontal plane separates front from back, and a transverse plane separates top from bottom and produces a cross section.

The body also has two main cavities. The dorsal cavity holds the brain and spinal cord. The ventral cavity holds the thoracic organs and, below the diaphragm, the abdominopelvic organs. Serous membranes line these spaces, with a parietal layer on the wall and a visceral layer on each organ, separated by a thin film of fluid that lets organs slide without friction.
